articles.title: Manchester United extend Fernandes’s contract to 2028; Raya back in Arsenal training – football live
articles.summary: ⚽ All the latest football news going into the weekend ⚽ Fixtures | Tables | Ten things to look out for | Mail Barry Let’s stay in quiz mode. Plenty of football questions in our weekly offering. I got the first seven right and then fell apart – a bit like Manchester City. Here’s the latest edition of Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend. Before you get to the infographic, a quiz question: which player is the second-top scorer in the Premier League over the last 12 months [Erling Haaland first, obvs]? Continue reading...
articles.content:
Newcastle: Sven Botman has been fined and banned from driving after pleading guilty to using a mobile phone at the while of his Land Rover on the A189 Haddricks Mill Road in Newcastle on 17 September.

The Newcastle United centre-back, who pleaded guilty at Newcastle Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday, was given six penalty points and disqualified from driving for six months as these were added to points he had already accrued. Botman was also fined £900, ordered to pay £400 costs and a £360 victim surcharge.

Sunderland: Not for the firs time this season, Regis Le Bris has been discussing the difficulties of balancing the bread and butter of the Premier League with Sunderland’s Europa League adventures. The Breton made six changes to the side that drew with Aston Villa for last night’s European draw with Jagiellonia Białystok and his new-look team could only draw with their Polish visitors.

“We respect the Europa League and we enjoy the competition, but the Premier League is our priority and we had to make a decision about selection,” he explained. “We know that if we kept the core and the spine of the squad we would have won, but we have to make changes because if we get injuries, we won’t win next week [in the Premier League]. It’s a shame but it’s fair.”

Hull City: Hot on the heels of their audacious smash-and-grab win over Brighton last Sunday, Hull travel to Premier League basement-dwellers Crystal Palace on Sunday and their head coach Sergej Jakirovic has confirmed that midfielder Tim Iroegbunam will be out for “about three months” after tearing a hammy during last weekend’s win.

“It is a big blow for us,” said the Bosnian. “We lost a very good player. He is very important for us, but we cannot change anything now. We have to be patient with him. We have to do everything to get him back again and we will do this.”

Sunderland: Having suffered the indignity of being booed off at the end of their 1-1 Europa League draw with the Polish side Jagiellonia Bialystok last night, Sunderland will be hoping for less of the same following their match against Tottenham Hotspur at the Stadium of Light on Sunday afternoon.

Regis Le Bris has told reporters that several of his players are struggling with illness following the outbreak of a virus in the camp. The illness has been suggested as an explanation for a dizzy spell suffered by Omar Alderete during last night’s game. “He has been assessed this morning and is fine but at the minute we have a few players on the edge with viruses and it is winter,” said Le Bris. “When it comes together it is more difficult to manage. It is always different for everyone, some of them can play and are doing really well but some are struggling because of their bodies and minds being different.”

While Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey are both back training after missing a few games with injury, Le Bris said it could be counter-productive to rush either player back. “They are running on the pitch now, which is good, but we don’t want to rush the process. For Brian and Granit, they want to play as soon as possible, so now it is a case of managing the situation. If you can’t sustain it the rest for the season, then it doesn’t make sense [to start them on Sunday].”

Aston Villa: Despite scoring four goals in a bonkers game they somehow contrived to only draw with Manchester United at Old Trafford, Aston Villa have been finding goals hard to come by recently. Unai Emery’s side have failed to score in four of their past six matches and have drawn blanks in their two most recent matches against Galatasaray and Sunderland.

“We are improving, getting better, feeling confident in some ways,” said Emery. “But there are still a lot of things to improve in a lot of ways. One of those ways is in the attacking third we need to produce something more.

“We need to try and get the balance offensively and defensively and get close to have chances to score. We are not winning and not losing. For some time we are not losing in the Premier League but we are not winning the last matches, especially at home.

“My idea with the players is to identify the good things positively that we are are doing and keep the good things there, and then add the things we need offensively. We are building the team and trying to identify the things quick that we need to improve.”

Villa are away at Ipswich on Saturday and have not lost in any of their past 11 visits to Portman Road.

Arsenal: In news pertaining to the Arsenal men’s team, Mikel Arteta has revealed that William Saliba, who has been sidelined since injuring his back while representing France during the World Cup, will be back in action in the very near future.

“He hasn’t played football for a long time,” he told reporters. “He can play a certain amount of minutes. He’s training well and he will have minutes in the next few games. And he will prove what he’s already done, that he’s an unbelievable player. Now he’s had more training [the number of minutes] will probably extend, but it will depend on the type of game and exposure that he will have throughout the game. He understands the situation, he’s just desperate to play, that’s for sure.”

Women’s football: Arsenal Dutch coach has left the club after less than two years in charge. Slegers led Arsenal to the Women’s Champions League title in 2025, but has left by “mutual consent” after a poor start to the current WSL campaign. Arsenal currently sit sixth in the table after 11 games, 12 points off the pace being set by Chelsea.

Manchester United: As well as confusing his audience while trying to explain the difference between being “good” and being “nice”, Mauricio Pochettino told reporters he expects to have a say in any player incomings and outgoings that are undertaken at United under his watch.

“In the future of course, but right now we are focused on trying to relate all of the ideas to the squad,” he said. “It’s not common sense if the head coach is not involved in situations that affect the build up of the squad. For me, that is a benefit for Manchester United. If I am not involved and I coach players that you don’t know or maybe you don’t want, or you don’t agree, that is not for me.

“I respect all ways to work but I am going to take my responsibility and everyone is going to know that I am going to be involved. That is what we were talking [about] in the last few days. Being the coach is not only to pick 11 players. It’s to assess and analyse the work behind about how you build. The responsibility is massive from the coaching staff.”

Time to hand over to the one and only Barry Glendenning , who will guide you through all Friday’s news and presser chat.

Andoni Iraola also talked about striker Alexander Isak, who took his goal tally for the season to 10 with a double against Club Brugge. “He has definitely improved a lot on the ball and without the ball,” said the Liverpool head coach.

“He is linking up play very well, technically he is a very nice player so I think we have to use him not just in the finishing side, he can be very important in our build up,” Iraola added. “I think he is understanding everything and is ready to learn and improve, and it is a good sign.” PA

A tricky one to call on Sunday? Brighton are nine points above Newcastle , but the Seagulls lost their last game at Hull, while Newcastle took a 2-2 draw from Arsenal. “Brighton are a top team, and we need to reach our limit,” says Matthias Jaissle of his team’s trip to the Amex.

Jaissle adds that he’s talked to “the lads” about the performance against Arsenal, and how to sustain the levels they showed in the second half. “After the 90 minutes, I had mixed feelings … there was frustration, but also excitement and pride about the second half. It’s about being more consistent, showing this performance more frequently.”

Mikel Arteta insists that the uncertainty over Manchester City’s punishment for breaking the Premier League’s financial rules will not overshadow their game against Arsenal.

City are still awaiting their fate after being found guilty of 114 breaches of regulations in September having lodged an appeal. Enzo Maresca’s side head to the Emirates on Sunday trailing Arsenal by six points after only 11 matches of the campaign.

“I hope that it doesn’t, because this is a process that is still open and not resolved and I wouldn’t know what is going to happen,” said Arteta when asked if the charges against City could be a distraction.

“I think when we have two teams at the level that they’re both in right now, with the quality of play that they have on that pitch, it’s a massive game and a big game to enjoy,” said Arteta, who added that retaining their title is “the only thing we should put the energy and the focus on”.

Arteta also refused to comment on whether emotions will be running high among supporters when City come to north London for the first time since being found guilty. “I don’t know. That’s something very individual and I don’t want to go there,” he said.

And now for Unai Emery , who has surprisingly positive things to say about Alejandro Garnacho. “He is training very well, his attitude is fantastic,” says Emery. “He was struggling when he joined, but now he is fit – if he’s not available, it’s because I have to choose from a lot of players. [But] he is much, much better.”

“Two months ago, he wasn’t fit enough to compete for a place,” the Aston Villa manager adds, and plays down talk of Garnacho returning to Chelsea in January. “I am focusing on tomorrow’s game [at Ipswich] … now we have 24 players and some will have to rotate.” Sounds like the door isn’t closed.

Over to Tottenham , where Roberto De Zerbi says Savio is likely to miss the team’s festive fixtures with a hamstring injury. “It’s a tough situation, but clubs all around Europe are suffering with injuries,” he adds.

Will Luca Williams-Barnett, who impressed against Ipswich, feature at the Stadium of Light on Sunday? “He can play in any game, but we need to analyse what’s best for him and for us,” says De Zerbi, urging caution over throwing the youngster in too often.

Coming up: Roberto De Zerbi has an update on Savio’s fitness, and Unai Emery has been discussing Alejandro Garnacho.

David Moyes is upbeat despite Everton ’s 4-0 defeat to Brentford on Monday. “I think the league is a bit like that, you can come up against a team having a great day.”

He says Jack Grealish is “in the mix” to play, and he expects another “close game” with Liverpool despite their rivals’ greater spending power and squad depth. He’s been impressed by Andoni Iraola’s start at Anfield, and says the derby “is a huge game, and always has been.”

On January transfer business, Moyes says: “I’m not concerned about anybody going out … we’re working behind the scenes but we need to get an idea of what (funds) are available.”

Here’s a little more from Mauricio Pochettino on his immediate priorities at Manchester United. “In only a few training sessions, the intensity and organisation. We cannot be perfect in three days, or two weeks … today we need to win, but work on the progression we need.

“The important thing is the players are very open to the idea to play in that way,” the United head coach added. “We need to improve of course, but like all styles, you need time to settle all the principles.”

Back to Premier League chat shortly, but here’s the full story on the violence at Thursday night’s Europa League game between Marseille and Levski Sofia.

Manchester United have activated their option to extend Bruno Fernandes’s contract by a year to 2028. The extension prevents Fernandes from agreeing a free summer transfer abroad in January, with further contract talks expected in the future.

Fernandes is a doubt for United’s home game against Brentford with a virus. The club captain told Sky Sports last week that contract negotiations have been “put to one side” amid the team’s shaky start to the season.

Arteta straight-bats a question about City’s charges affecting their form, and doesn’t agree that an Arsenal win on Sunday would end City’s title hopes – but does say that home games against big teams are crucial.

“I know Enzo personally, he’s a phenomenal guy who breathes football,” he says of Maresca, and adds that he’s “not worried” about a slight slowdown in Arsenal’s goalscoring. Is he expecting home supporters to follow Liverpool fans’ lead in regard to City’s charges on Sunday? Unsurprisingly, he’s not getting into that.

Here’s Mikel Arteta , who is asked whether David Raya could feature against Manchester City – it’s a maybe at this stage, but he confirms the keeper is back in training after suffering an injury against Newcastle.

It’s 27 November and I’ve seen that Sky Christmas ad 1,057 times already Ross County have already scored 102 goals this season. Ewan Murray has more on the Highland high-flyers tearing up the Scottish third tier.

Nottingham Forest host Chelsea tonight in a meeting of two teams running low on positive vibes.

“Chelsea are a team that want to play football … very high-quality players, some injury concerns, and they struggled with Leeds’ physicality,” says Oliver Glasner, perhaps throwing in some big words to make a point.

“It’s not what we’ve done, it’s what we can do,” says Xabi Alonso. “We need to show a competitive reaction, show much better, do much better. It’s clear now [what Chelsea need to do], we just need to execute it.”

“I know this is a very big game, and I hope I can enjoy it,” Iraola says of his first Merseyside derby. He also praises David Moyes, who was in the West Ham dugout when Iraola made his Bournemouth debut. “He spoke to me afterwards and has offered me lots of advice,” Iraola adds.

And now Liverpool’s Andoni Iraola , who says Cody Gakpo will not be available for Sunday’s derby trip to Everton. As for Victor Muñoz, scans on his knee have been positive and the player feels ready to play, but Iraola suggests he may need more time to recover.

Staying in Manchester, here’s Mauricio Pochettino , who makes his Old Trafford bow on Saturday against Brentford. “We have to use our experience and quality to make sure we can win,” he says, making it all sound so simple.

“There’s a difference between being nice and good,” he continues. “I am not nice – and we have to be good.” A bit opaque, but fair enough. Pochettino also confirms that Bruno Fernandes is ill, and will undergo a fitness test tomorrow.

“We don’t know (if he will be available),” Pochettino said. “He’s affected by a virus from Portugal. He finished the game a little bit with a problem, and today he could not be part of the training session. We’ll see.”

“We are going to see during the day and tomorrow how he wakes up and see. We are not going to take any risk.”

Enzo Maresca is early to his Manchester City presser; he says there is “no reason” his side can’t win at the Emirates on Sunday despite their poor run of form – and said he’s not worried about recent results.

“Everyone was thinking there would be no transition, like I’m a magician,” Maresca adds. “Of course there will be – we have a lot of new players, there will be transition. I’m not worried at all.” He also reports that Antoine Semenyo is “very close” to a return from injury.

Maresca also played down any concerns over Erling Haaland’s mood. “For sure he is not happy because we are not winning games. But it is not just Erling. Everyone is on the same page.

“He has been good. He has been normal since day one. Two or three weeks ago, he was dancing inside the pitch and in the training sessions. He is happy. It is normal that results affect the mood a little bit but I don’t see any problem with Erling. He is a winner.”

The Curious Case of Alejandro Garnacho is a major talking point for Aston Villa supporters and the club’s director of football, Damian Vidagany, addressed the issue at a fans’ forum on Thursday. Garnacho has played just 34 minutes in the Premier League this season and is yet to start a Villa match in any competition. The 22-year-old was left out of Villa’s squad at Galatasaray on Tuesday, with Unai Emery preferring to name 11 substitutes rather than include the Chelsea loanee.

“At this moment in time the situation is that Unai Emery is picking other players, he’s decided not to put [Garnacho] in the squad,” said Vidagany, a longstanding confidant of Emery. “This can change or not – I don’t know. It will depend mainly on the performance of the player, because we are a football club that tries to be efficient with the resources that we have. But above that, there is not any question that Unai Emery has the right and the full power to decide which players are in the squad or not.”

Prosecutors have opened two investigations into fan violence at Thursday’s Europa League match between Marseille and Levski Sofia, while Uefa has announced disciplinary investigations into clashes at that game and at Besiktas v Hapoel Be’er Sheva in Batumi, Georgia.

The ​Marseille prosecutor’s office have said their investigation concerns aggravated assault by Marseille supporters and the other incitement ⁠to hatred over Nazi salutes and ⁠other provocations by visiting Bulgarian fans.

Images from the ⁠Stade Vélodrome showed masked fans wielding improvised weapons and metal pipes during a brawl. A Reuters photographer said the clashes began after a visiting supporter made a Nazi salute. Levski Sofia have claimed their fans were attacked first by Marseille supporters.

“CCTV footage is ⁠currently being analysed,” the Marseille prosecutor’s office said in a statement announcing the investigations. Reuters

The former Iceland goalkeeper Ingvar Jónsson has died at the age of 37. His death was announced by his former club, Víkingur, on Thursday. Jónsson, who won eight caps was part of his country’s Euro 2016 squad, had reportedly been diagnosed with cancer earlier this year.

“It is with great sorrow and deep sadness that we announce that our dear friend and teammate Ingvar Jónsson passed away on 25 November in the arms of his loved ones,” the Icelandic club said in a statement.

“The club and all of Víkingur are thinking of his family and loved ones. We send them our deepest condolences.”

Sheffield Wednesday have invited Hallam FC season-ticket holders to attend Saturday’s League One match against Reading free of charge.

Founded in 1860, Sheffield side Hallam have withdrawn from this season’s Northern Premier League East due to serious financial issues. The world’s second-oldest football club behind Sheffield FC, Hallam’s Sandygate home is the oldest football ground anywhere on earth that is still in use.

“We recognise this is an incredibly difficult time for everyone associated with Hallam FC, particularly its supporters, volunteers and wider community,” a Sheffield Wednesday statement read. “Football clubs are at the heart of their communities and while this is only a small gesture, we hope it provides Hallam supporters with an opportunity to enjoy a game of football this weekend.”

We’re approaching press conference rush hour, with no fewer than nine Premier League managers speaking at 1.30pm (GMT). They include David Moyes and Andoni Iraola , who meet in Sunday’s Merseyside derby, plus Mikel Arteta and Enzo Maresca before Arsenal v Manchester City.

We’ll also hear from Mauricio Pochettino, Roberto De Zerbi, Matthias Jassle, Gary O’Neil and Régis Le Bris . Hull manager Sergej Jakirovic is speaking at 1pm, with Aston Villa’s Unai Emery up at 2pm.

The Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has insisted Calvin Bassey is going nowhere in January, amid links with a move to Manchester United.

“I’m so happy with Calvin, and obviously he is not on sale,” Arbeloa said in his Friday press conference. “No chance he can leave this club in January and I think he is happy here.”

“He is one of our captains, he is one of our leaders,” Arbeloa added. “It is normal so many clubs are interested in him, it is good for him and good for us. It means he is performing really well. We are working on a new contract and I hope he can sign as soon as possible.”

Bruno Fernandes has missed Manchester United training today due to illness, the club have confirmed. “The captain is feeling a bit under the weather and is, therefore, being protected ahead of the clash with Brentford,” reports the club’s official website. Fernandes scored both goals in Wednesday’s 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting.

The WSL2 side Ipswich Town have signed the England youth international Princess Ademiluyi from American NWSL outfit Gotham FC on a three-and-a-half-year deal for a new club-record fee.

It follows the 20-year-old striker’s impressive loan spell, during which time she has scored seven goals in 19 games in all competitions. Third-placed Ipswich, who are just three points off an automatic promotion spot, were very keen to make her stay more permanent.

Sean Burt, Ipswich’s women’s technical director, told the club website: “Securing a player of her calibre from one of the biggest clubs in world football is a real statement of our ambition, particularly given the significant impact she has already had on both the squad and our performances on the pitch.”

It’s all eyes on Sweden this weekend, with the title race coming down to Sunday’s final round of games. Sirius , the long-time surprise leaders , have struggled since striker Robbie Ure left for Sevilla – allowing Hammarby to overtake them on goal difference.

Stockholm side Hammarby, who are part-owned by Zlatan Ibrahimovic, can seal their second-ever title (and first since 2001) with victory at sixth-placed Västerås. Sirius, who hail from Uppsala, go to IFK Göteborg and need to better Hammarby’s result to claim their first-ever championship. Reporting by AP

What’s Ryan Fraser been up to lately, I hear you ask. Well, the former Bournemouth winger hit this scorcher to put Macarthur top of Australia’s A-League …

“How long do you assess that Poch will last at the Theatre of Nightmares? Two red cards (one rescinded), one loss (hiding) and one draw is not a promising start to a new regime,” writes Krishna.

It’s hard to draw too many conclusions from the first two games, riddled as they were with individual errors. There were signs of improvement against Sporting; I think tomorrow’s home game against Brentford will offer us a clearer picture.

With Bayern’s injuries piling up, could Dortmund mount an unexpected title challenge? Niko Kovac’s side are yet to fully find their groove this season, but are still unbeaten after 10 games.

Hello everyone – a big hand for my esteemed colleague, Dave Tindall. There’s a whole lot of press conference fun coming up, but you can prep for the Premier League weekend here:

Bayern Munich’s attacking options are thinning out. Vincent Kompany has confirmed Michael Olise will miss Saturday’s Bundesliga game against Hamburg with a bruised foot, joining Harry Kane on the sidelines.

Both were hurt in last week’s 1-1 draw with Köln; Kane has had surgery on torn ankle ligaments and is expected to be out for around three months.

With no recognised striker available, Kompany fielded midfielder Konrad Laimer up front at Lille in midweek, without success.

It’s been a sharp turn for a club that swept the domestic trophies in Germany last season. Since the Köln draw – Bayern’s fourth stalemate in the Bundesliga already – things have gone south.

A makeshift side surrendered a 1-0 lead at Lille on Wednesday, conceding twice in four second-half minutes to slip to a first Champions League defeat of the campaign and leave their top-eight hopes hanging by a thread.

They sit 15th in the league phase, while at home they’re second, two points behind Borussia Dortmund, ahead of Saturday’s trip to Hamburg.

Daniel Farke has been talking about snoods. No, really. The Leeds boss isn’t having big-time Charlies knocking about the place and was quick to clamp down after he spotted a staff member still celebrating last Saturday’s 4-1 win at Chelsea during this week’s first training session.

I accept it’s cold and you have to put yourself in warm clothes, but instead of wearing a hat – a hat is totally fine – he was wearing a snood over his head, like this 20-year-old creative number 10.

It was as if he had have won the game at Chelsea on his own. Well, it was a long working day for him that day, I made sure.

He was helping our kit men, and from now on he stays in shorts and t-shirt until the end of January on the pitch outside.

If anyone thinks ‘we are too good for this’ and can be cool like a 20-year-old number 10, like one of my staff members, I will make sure that everyone is also back to work and doesn’t enjoy himself too much.

But I don’t have to do anything with our supporters. They can even come with a snood over their head and enjoy themselves, no problem at all.

The Yorkshire Post said Farke was half-jokingly horrified earlier in the season when Ao Tanaka wore gloves in training before the weather had turned cold.

Some Optas for tonight’s Premier League game. They don’t make great reading for either side!

● Since a run of three consecutive wins in April/May last season (the third of which was against Chelsea), Nottingham Forest have won just two of their last 14 Premier League games (D5 L7).

● Since the start of March, no side has lost more Premier League games than Chelsea (13), while among ever present sides only Crystal Palace (17) have earned fewer points than the Blues in that time (23).

Fifa news via Nick Ames: a number of past and present Fifa employees have received letters requesting they attend interviews for a congressional investigation into the global governing body sparked by the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal.

Letters were sent on Wednesday to a number of staff along with a handful of former employees who held senior positions.

They have been asked by Democrats on the House judiciary committee to give evidence as efforts gather pace to examine Gianni Infantino’s failed FFE scheme along with links between Fifa and the Trump administration.

Should recipients agree, the voluntary interviews could commence as soon as next week.

Five Levski Sofia supporters were taken to hospital after violence before last night’s Europa League game at Marseille . Both the French and Bulgarian presidents are blaming the home fans.

The lead-up to the match at the Stade Vélodrome was marred by confrontations in the stands between the two sets of fans, including the throwing of projectiles and flares.

French president Emmanuel Macron condemned “in the strongest possible terms... acts of violence targeting Bulgarian fans”, the Élysée Palace said. The Bulgarian president, Iliana Iotova, said it was “unacceptable” and “shocking”.

“The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world,” she said in a statement on Facebook. “Everyone should be able to support their team without being afraid for their safety.”

Macron spoke to his Bulgarian counterpart on the sidelines of a European summit in Brussels, assuring her that “these acts would not go unpunished”, the Élysée said.

Several hundred Marseille fans ran from the stand where they were situated about 10 minutes before kick-off, appearing to pursue a group of Bulgarian supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, where around 500 Levski fans were gathered.

“Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder,” the Marseille police prefecture told AFP. “Six others were treated on site for various wounds.” AFP

A week is a long time in football. With a midweek round of action in the Premier League , Manchester United could theoretically be somewhere in mid-table if their upcoming Saturday-Wednesday-Saturday schedule goes extremely well. Okay, that’s a big ask for a team without a top-flight win since (checks notes) August but home games against Brentford and Coventry either side of a midweek trip to Newcastle offer new boss Mauricio Pochettino the chance to build upon some promising signs in the 2-2 draw with Sporting.

Then again, United may be stranded at the bottom if it all goes belly up. The flurry of action begins tonight with Nottingham Forest hosting Chelsea and builds towards Sunday’s showdown at the Emirates where leaders Arsenal take on Manchester City.

Those two were held to home draws in the Champions League on Tuesday but it was a strong night in Europe for the English teams on Thursday. Well, apart from Sunderland. We’ll have reflections on last night’s games, all the weekend build-up and much more! Let’s go!

Let’s stay in quiz mode. Plenty of football questions in our weekly offering. I got the first seven right and then fell apart – a bit like Manchester City.

Here’s the latest edition of Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend. Before you get to the infographic, a quiz question: which player is the second-top scorer in the Premier League over the last 12 months [Erling Haaland first, obvs]?

Manchester United will launch “The Check-In”, a mental health and suicide prevention initiative, when Brentford visit Old Trafford on Saturday. The initiative, which will take place at 10 home games this season, is in conjunction with the Premier League and the Salford-based support group Talk About It Mate.

It will offer a “safe and welcoming space where supporters can drop in, have a chat with trained counsellors and volunteers, and find out more about further support”, a press release from United stated.

Rhys Bennett, who captained United’s under-18s to the 2021-22 FA Youth Cup and is now at Fleetwood, lost his father, David, to suicide last year. The 23-year-old recently attended a Talk About It Mate session at Salford Boys Club and urged anyone who feels it may help to attend Saturday’s session (starts 12pm) at the Apollo pitch in front of the Sir Alex Ferguson stand.

“It’s one of the most powerful things I’ve ever done,” said the defender. “I play football for a living and it can be hard performing every day in a high-pressure environment. I was a bit nervous but within five minutes, you realise that there’s no judgment and you can talk about how you’re really feeling, which only makes you stronger in day-to-day life.”

The weekend Premier League action starts tonight with Nottingham Forest hosting Chelsea. With Forest’s Liam Delap about to take on the team he left after just one season, here’s Jacob Steinberg on how the constant turnover of players and staff has made consistency an elusive quality at Stamford Bridge.

Brentford boss Keith Andrews is a big fan of his Manchester United counterpart Mauricio Pochettino. Expect a warm embrace before Saturday’s showdown at Old Trafford and perhaps a cold handshake afterwards if the sixth-placed Bees condemn United to a sixth Premier League defeat of the season. Here’s Andrews:

He [Pochettino] is someone that we know. I studied his teams quite a lot in my coaching journey and had a lot of admiration for him. Even before his Tottenham team, it was his Southampton team.

You can see traits of what he is as a manager and what he would like to push into his new United team. Of course, you have got to balance that with where they are currently and what they have been doing.

I think you can see the little transition, even though it has been seven or eight minutes against Liverpool [before Leny Yoro’s now overturned red card] and then the game against Sporting Lisbon, so we will expect a very well-organised Man United side.

If you want a bit of cricket blog action, may I point you here. England taking Aussie wickets for fun mainly thanks to a five-fer from Jamie Overton.

Here’s a fascinating read – Donald McRae’s interview with Eric Cantona. Words are fantastic and so are the photos! A new documentary on the Frenchman is coming our way soon. Details of tickets and cinema timings are in the article.

Maybe I’m a good person, but I can also be a flower of evil. It’s the first time in my life I’ve realised this. I am a flower of evil, and I find it very beautiful.

Bournemouth’s form figures look like bunting – WWWWWWWWWW – and another flag went up last night. The Cherries made it 10 wins in succession in all competitions with a come-from-behind win at Spanish side Celta Vigo. And they did so despite having a man sent off in the first half. Here’s news of that one, plus a round-up of events elsewhere in the Europa League.

After taking four points off Chelsea and Aston Villa to move off the bottom of the table, Sunderland were expected to beat Jagiellonia Bialystok last night. It didn’t happen. Louise Taylor was at the Stadium of Light.

Thomas Frank has his first win as Crystal Palace boss. And it came after they were 1-0 down to Real Sociedad with 17 minutes left of Thursday’s Europa League clash at Selhurst Park. Here’s Ed Aarons on a night of second-half twists.
paragraphs: Newcastle: Sven Botman has been fined and banned from driving after pleading guilty to using a mobile phone at the while of his Land Rover on the A189 Haddricks Mill Road in Newcastle on 17 September.

The Newcastle United centre-back, who pleaded guilty at Newcastle Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday, was given six penalty points and disqualified from driving for six months as these were added to points he had already accrued. Botman was also fined £900, ordered to pay £400 costs and a £360 victim surcharge.

Sunderland: Not for the firs time this season, Regis Le Bris has been discussing the difficulties of balancing the bread and butter of the Premier League with Sunderland’s Europa League adventures. The Breton made six changes to the side that drew with Aston Villa for last night’s European draw with Jagiellonia Białystok and his new-look team could only draw with their Polish visitors.

“We respect the Europa League and we enjoy the competition, but the Premier League is our priority and we had to make a decision about selection,” he explained. “We know that if we kept the core and the spine of the squad we would have won, but we have to make changes because if we get injuries, we won’t win next week [in the Premier League]. It’s a shame but it’s fair.”

Hull City: Hot on the heels of their audacious smash-and-grab win over Brighton last Sunday, Hull travel to Premier League basement-dwellers Crystal Palace on Sunday and their head coach Sergej Jakirovic has confirmed that midfielder Tim Iroegbunam will be out for “about three months” after tearing a hammy during last weekend’s win.

“It is a big blow for us,” said the Bosnian. “We lost a very good player. He is very important for us, but we cannot change anything now. We have to be patient with him. We have to do everything to get him back again and we will do this.”

Sunderland: Having suffered the indignity of being booed off at the end of their 1-1 Europa League draw with the Polish side Jagiellonia Bialystok last night, Sunderland will be hoping for less of the same following their match against Tottenham Hotspur at the Stadium of Light on Sunday afternoon.

Regis Le Bris has told reporters that several of his players are struggling with illness following the outbreak of a virus in the camp. The illness has been suggested as an explanation for a dizzy spell suffered by Omar Alderete during last night’s game. “He has been assessed this morning and is fine but at the minute we have a few players on the edge with viruses and it is winter,” said Le Bris. “When it comes together it is more difficult to manage. It is always different for everyone, some of them can play and are doing really well but some are struggling because of their bodies and minds being different.”

While Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey are both back training after missing a few games with injury, Le Bris said it could be counter-productive to rush either player back. “They are running on the pitch now, which is good, but we don’t want to rush the process. For Brian and Granit, they want to play as soon as possible, so now it is a case of managing the situation. If you can’t sustain it the rest for the season, then it doesn’t make sense [to start them on Sunday].”

Aston Villa: Despite scoring four goals in a bonkers game they somehow contrived to only draw with Manchester United at Old Trafford, Aston Villa have been finding goals hard to come by recently. Unai Emery’s side have failed to score in four of their past six matches and have drawn blanks in their two most recent matches against Galatasaray and Sunderland.

“We are improving, getting better, feeling confident in some ways,” said Emery. “But there are still a lot of things to improve in a lot of ways. One of those ways is in the attacking third we need to produce something more.

“We need to try and get the balance offensively and defensively and get close to have chances to score. We are not winning and not losing. For some time we are not losing in the Premier League but we are not winning the last matches, especially at home.

“My idea with the players is to identify the good things positively that we are are doing and keep the good things there, and then add the things we need offensively. We are building the team and trying to identify the things quick that we need to improve.”
Villa are away at Ipswich on Saturday and have not lost in any of their past 11 visits to Portman Road.

Arsenal: In news pertaining to the Arsenal men’s team, Mikel Arteta has revealed that William Saliba, who has been sidelined since injuring his back while representing France during the World Cup, will be back in action in the very near future.

“He hasn’t played football for a long time,” he told reporters. “He can play a certain amount of minutes. He’s training well and he will have minutes in the next few games. And he will prove what he’s already done, that he’s an unbelievable player. Now he’s had more training [the number of minutes] will probably extend, but it will depend on the type of game and exposure that he will have throughout the game. He understands the situation, he’s just desperate to play, that’s for sure.”

Women’s football: Arsenal Dutch coach has left the club after less than two years in charge. Slegers led Arsenal to the Women’s Champions League title in 2025, but has left by “mutual consent” after a poor start to the current WSL campaign. Arsenal currently sit sixth in the table after 11 games, 12 points off the pace being set by Chelsea.

Manchester United: As well as confusing his audience while trying to explain the difference between being “good” and being “nice”, Mauricio Pochettino told reporters he expects to have a say in any player incomings and outgoings that are undertaken at United under his watch.

“In the future of course, but right now we are focused on trying to relate all of the ideas to the squad,” he said. “It’s not common sense if the head coach is not involved in situations that affect the build up of the squad. For me, that is a benefit for Manchester United. If I am not involved and I coach players that you don’t know or maybe you don’t want, or you don’t agree, that is not for me.

“I respect all ways to work but I am going to take my responsibility and everyone is going to know that I am going to be involved. That is what we were talking [about] in the last few days. Being the coach is not only to pick 11 players. It’s to assess and analyse the work behind about how you build. The responsibility is massive from the coaching staff.”
Time to hand over to the one and only Barry Glendenning , who will guide you through all Friday’s news and presser chat.

Andoni Iraola also talked about striker Alexander Isak, who took his goal tally for the season to 10 with a double against Club Brugge. “He has definitely improved a lot on the ball and without the ball,” said the Liverpool head coach.

“He is linking up play very well, technically he is a very nice player so I think we have to use him not just in the finishing side, he can be very important in our build up,” Iraola added. “I think he is understanding everything and is ready to learn and improve, and it is a good sign.” PA

A tricky one to call on Sunday? Brighton are nine points above Newcastle , but the Seagulls lost their last game at Hull, while Newcastle took a 2-2 draw from Arsenal. “Brighton are a top team, and we need to reach our limit,” says Matthias Jaissle of his team’s trip to the Amex.

Jaissle adds that he’s talked to “the lads” about the performance against Arsenal, and how to sustain the levels they showed in the second half. “After the 90 minutes, I had mixed feelings … there was frustration, but also excitement and pride about the second half. It’s about being more consistent, showing this performance more frequently.”
Mikel Arteta insists that the uncertainty over Manchester City’s punishment for breaking the Premier League’s financial rules will not overshadow their game against Arsenal.

City are still awaiting their fate after being found guilty of 114 breaches of regulations in September having lodged an appeal. Enzo Maresca’s side head to the Emirates on Sunday trailing Arsenal by six points after only 11 matches of the campaign.

“I hope that it doesn’t, because this is a process that is still open and not resolved and I wouldn’t know what is going to happen,” said Arteta when asked if the charges against City could be a distraction.

“I think when we have two teams at the level that they’re both in right now, with the quality of play that they have on that pitch, it’s a massive game and a big game to enjoy,” said Arteta, who added that retaining their title is “the only thing we should put the energy and the focus on”.

Arteta also refused to comment on whether emotions will be running high among supporters when City come to north London for the first time since being found guilty. “I don’t know. That’s something very individual and I don’t want to go there,” he said.

And now for Unai Emery , who has surprisingly positive things to say about Alejandro Garnacho. “He is training very well, his attitude is fantastic,” says Emery. “He was struggling when he joined, but now he is fit – if he’s not available, it’s because I have to choose from a lot of players. [But] he is much, much better.”

“Two months ago, he wasn’t fit enough to compete for a place,” the Aston Villa manager adds, and plays down talk of Garnacho returning to Chelsea in January. “I am focusing on tomorrow’s game [at Ipswich] … now we have 24 players and some will have to rotate.” Sounds like the door isn’t closed.

Over to Tottenham , where Roberto De Zerbi says Savio is likely to miss the team’s festive fixtures with a hamstring injury. “It’s a tough situation, but clubs all around Europe are suffering with injuries,” he adds.

Will Luca Williams-Barnett, who impressed against Ipswich, feature at the Stadium of Light on Sunday? “He can play in any game, but we need to analyse what’s best for him and for us,” says De Zerbi, urging caution over throwing the youngster in too often.
Coming up: Roberto De Zerbi has an update on Savio’s fitness, and Unai Emery has been discussing Alejandro Garnacho.
David Moyes is upbeat despite Everton ’s 4-0 defeat to Brentford on Monday. “I think the league is a bit like that, you can come up against a team having a great day.”

He says Jack Grealish is “in the mix” to play, and he expects another “close game” with Liverpool despite their rivals’ greater spending power and squad depth. He’s been impressed by Andoni Iraola’s start at Anfield, and says the derby “is a huge game, and always has been.”
On January transfer business, Moyes says: “I’m not concerned about anybody going out … we’re working behind the scenes but we need to get an idea of what (funds) are available.”

Here’s a little more from Mauricio Pochettino on his immediate priorities at Manchester United. “In only a few training sessions, the intensity and organisation. We cannot be perfect in three days, or two weeks … today we need to win, but work on the progression we need.

“The important thing is the players are very open to the idea to play in that way,” the United head coach added. “We need to improve of course, but like all styles, you need time to settle all the principles.”
Back to Premier League chat shortly, but here’s the full story on the violence at Thursday night’s Europa League game between Marseille and Levski Sofia.

Manchester United have activated their option to extend Bruno Fernandes’s contract by a year to 2028. The extension prevents Fernandes from agreeing a free summer transfer abroad in January, with further contract talks expected in the future.

Fernandes is a doubt for United’s home game against Brentford with a virus. The club captain told Sky Sports last week that contract negotiations have been “put to one side” amid the team’s shaky start to the season.

Arteta straight-bats a question about City’s charges affecting their form, and doesn’t agree that an Arsenal win on Sunday would end City’s title hopes – but does say that home games against big teams are crucial.

“I know Enzo personally, he’s a phenomenal guy who breathes football,” he says of Maresca, and adds that he’s “not worried” about a slight slowdown in Arsenal’s goalscoring. Is he expecting home supporters to follow Liverpool fans’ lead in regard to City’s charges on Sunday? Unsurprisingly, he’s not getting into that.

Here’s Mikel Arteta , who is asked whether David Raya could feature against Manchester City – it’s a maybe at this stage, but he confirms the keeper is back in training after suffering an injury against Newcastle.

It’s 27 November and I’ve seen that Sky Christmas ad 1,057 times already Ross County have already scored 102 goals this season. Ewan Murray has more on the Highland high-flyers tearing up the Scottish third tier.
Nottingham Forest host Chelsea tonight in a meeting of two teams running low on positive vibes.

“Chelsea are a team that want to play football … very high-quality players, some injury concerns, and they struggled with Leeds’ physicality,” says Oliver Glasner, perhaps throwing in some big words to make a point.

“It’s not what we’ve done, it’s what we can do,” says Xabi Alonso. “We need to show a competitive reaction, show much better, do much better. It’s clear now [what Chelsea need to do], we just need to execute it.”

“I know this is a very big game, and I hope I can enjoy it,” Iraola says of his first Merseyside derby. He also praises David Moyes, who was in the West Ham dugout when Iraola made his Bournemouth debut. “He spoke to me afterwards and has offered me lots of advice,” Iraola adds.

And now Liverpool’s Andoni Iraola , who says Cody Gakpo will not be available for Sunday’s derby trip to Everton. As for Victor Muñoz, scans on his knee have been positive and the player feels ready to play, but Iraola suggests he may need more time to recover.

Staying in Manchester, here’s Mauricio Pochettino , who makes his Old Trafford bow on Saturday against Brentford. “We have to use our experience and quality to make sure we can win,” he says, making it all sound so simple.

“There’s a difference between being nice and good,” he continues. “I am not nice – and we have to be good.” A bit opaque, but fair enough. Pochettino also confirms that Bruno Fernandes is ill, and will undergo a fitness test tomorrow.

“We don’t know (if he will be available),” Pochettino said. “He’s affected by a virus from Portugal. He finished the game a little bit with a problem, and today he could not be part of the training session. We’ll see.”
“We are going to see during the day and tomorrow how he wakes up and see. We are not going to take any risk.”

Enzo Maresca is early to his Manchester City presser; he says there is “no reason” his side can’t win at the Emirates on Sunday despite their poor run of form – and said he’s not worried about recent results.

“Everyone was thinking there would be no transition, like I’m a magician,” Maresca adds. “Of course there will be – we have a lot of new players, there will be transition. I’m not worried at all.” He also reports that Antoine Semenyo is “very close” to a return from injury.
Maresca also played down any concerns over Erling Haaland’s mood. “For sure he is not happy because we are not winning games. But it is not just Erling. Everyone is on the same page.

“He has been good. He has been normal since day one. Two or three weeks ago, he was dancing inside the pitch and in the training sessions. He is happy. It is normal that results affect the mood a little bit but I don’t see any problem with Erling. He is a winner.”

The Curious Case of Alejandro Garnacho is a major talking point for Aston Villa supporters and the club’s director of football, Damian Vidagany, addressed the issue at a fans’ forum on Thursday. Garnacho has played just 34 minutes in the Premier League this season and is yet to start a Villa match in any competition. The 22-year-old was left out of Villa’s squad at Galatasaray on Tuesday, with Unai Emery preferring to name 11 substitutes rather than include the Chelsea loanee.

“At this moment in time the situation is that Unai Emery is picking other players, he’s decided not to put [Garnacho] in the squad,” said Vidagany, a longstanding confidant of Emery. “This can change or not – I don’t know. It will depend mainly on the performance of the player, because we are a football club that tries to be efficient with the resources that we have. But above that, there is not any question that Unai Emery has the right and the full power to decide which players are in the squad or not.”

Prosecutors have opened two investigations into fan violence at Thursday’s Europa League match between Marseille and Levski Sofia, while Uefa has announced disciplinary investigations into clashes at that game and at Besiktas v Hapoel Be’er Sheva in Batumi, Georgia.

The ​Marseille prosecutor’s office have said their investigation concerns aggravated assault by Marseille supporters and the other incitement ⁠to hatred over Nazi salutes and ⁠other provocations by visiting Bulgarian fans.

Images from the ⁠Stade Vélodrome showed masked fans wielding improvised weapons and metal pipes during a brawl. A Reuters photographer said the clashes began after a visiting supporter made a Nazi salute. Levski Sofia have claimed their fans were attacked first by Marseille supporters.
“CCTV footage is ⁠currently being analysed,” the Marseille prosecutor’s office said in a statement announcing the investigations. Reuters

The former Iceland goalkeeper Ingvar Jónsson has died at the age of 37. His death was announced by his former club, Víkingur, on Thursday. Jónsson, who won eight caps was part of his country’s Euro 2016 squad, had reportedly been diagnosed with cancer earlier this year.

“It is with great sorrow and deep sadness that we announce that our dear friend and teammate Ingvar Jónsson passed away on 25 November in the arms of his loved ones,” the Icelandic club said in a statement.
“The club and all of Víkingur are thinking of his family and loved ones. We send them our deepest condolences.”
Sheffield Wednesday have invited Hallam FC season-ticket holders to attend Saturday’s League One match against Reading free of charge.

Founded in 1860, Sheffield side Hallam have withdrawn from this season’s Northern Premier League East due to serious financial issues. The world’s second-oldest football club behind Sheffield FC, Hallam’s Sandygate home is the oldest football ground anywhere on earth that is still in use.

“We recognise this is an incredibly difficult time for everyone associated with Hallam FC, particularly its supporters, volunteers and wider community,” a Sheffield Wednesday statement read. “Football clubs are at the heart of their communities and while this is only a small gesture, we hope it provides Hallam supporters with an opportunity to enjoy a game of football this weekend.”

We’re approaching press conference rush hour, with no fewer than nine Premier League managers speaking at 1.30pm (GMT). They include David Moyes and Andoni Iraola , who meet in Sunday’s Merseyside derby, plus Mikel Arteta and Enzo Maresca before Arsenal v Manchester City.
We’ll also hear from Mauricio Pochettino, Roberto De Zerbi, Matthias Jassle, Gary O’Neil and Régis Le Bris . Hull manager Sergej Jakirovic is speaking at 1pm, with Aston Villa’s Unai Emery up at 2pm.
The Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has insisted Calvin Bassey is going nowhere in January, amid links with a move to Manchester United.
“I’m so happy with Calvin, and obviously he is not on sale,” Arbeloa said in his Friday press conference. “No chance he can leave this club in January and I think he is happy here.”

“He is one of our captains, he is one of our leaders,” Arbeloa added. “It is normal so many clubs are interested in him, it is good for him and good for us. It means he is performing really well. We are working on a new contract and I hope he can sign as soon as possible.”

Bruno Fernandes has missed Manchester United training today due to illness, the club have confirmed. “The captain is feeling a bit under the weather and is, therefore, being protected ahead of the clash with Brentford,” reports the club’s official website. Fernandes scored both goals in Wednesday’s 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting.
The WSL2 side Ipswich Town have signed the England youth international Princess Ademiluyi from American NWSL outfit Gotham FC on a three-and-a-half-year deal for a new club-record fee.

It follows the 20-year-old striker’s impressive loan spell, during which time she has scored seven goals in 19 games in all competitions. Third-placed Ipswich, who are just three points off an automatic promotion spot, were very keen to make her stay more permanent.

Sean Burt, Ipswich’s women’s technical director, told the club website: “Securing a player of her calibre from one of the biggest clubs in world football is a real statement of our ambition, particularly given the significant impact she has already had on both the squad and our performances on the pitch.”

It’s all eyes on Sweden this weekend, with the title race coming down to Sunday’s final round of games. Sirius , the long-time surprise leaders , have struggled since striker Robbie Ure left for Sevilla – allowing Hammarby to overtake them on goal difference.

Stockholm side Hammarby, who are part-owned by Zlatan Ibrahimovic, can seal their second-ever title (and first since 2001) with victory at sixth-placed Västerås. Sirius, who hail from Uppsala, go to IFK Göteborg and need to better Hammarby’s result to claim their first-ever championship. Reporting by AP
What’s Ryan Fraser been up to lately, I hear you ask. Well, the former Bournemouth winger hit this scorcher to put Macarthur top of Australia’s A-League …
“How long do you assess that Poch will last at the Theatre of Nightmares? Two red cards (one rescinded), one loss (hiding) and one draw is not a promising start to a new regime,” writes Krishna.

It’s hard to draw too many conclusions from the first two games, riddled as they were with individual errors. There were signs of improvement against Sporting; I think tomorrow’s home game against Brentford will offer us a clearer picture.
With Bayern’s injuries piling up, could Dortmund mount an unexpected title challenge? Niko Kovac’s side are yet to fully find their groove this season, but are still unbeaten after 10 games.
Hello everyone – a big hand for my esteemed colleague, Dave Tindall. There’s a whole lot of press conference fun coming up, but you can prep for the Premier League weekend here:

Bayern Munich’s attacking options are thinning out. Vincent Kompany has confirmed Michael Olise will miss Saturday’s Bundesliga game against Hamburg with a bruised foot, joining Harry Kane on the sidelines.
Both were hurt in last week’s 1-1 draw with Köln; Kane has had surgery on torn ankle ligaments and is expected to be out for around three months.
With no recognised striker available, Kompany fielded midfielder Konrad Laimer up front at Lille in midweek, without success.
It’s been a sharp turn for a club that swept the domestic trophies in Germany last season. Since the Köln draw – Bayern’s fourth stalemate in the Bundesliga already – things have gone south.

A makeshift side surrendered a 1-0 lead at Lille on Wednesday, conceding twice in four second-half minutes to slip to a first Champions League defeat of the campaign and leave their top-eight hopes hanging by a thread.
They sit 15th in the league phase, while at home they’re second, two points behind Borussia Dortmund, ahead of Saturday’s trip to Hamburg.

Daniel Farke has been talking about snoods. No, really. The Leeds boss isn’t having big-time Charlies knocking about the place and was quick to clamp down after he spotted a staff member still celebrating last Saturday’s 4-1 win at Chelsea during this week’s first training session.
I accept it’s cold and you have to put yourself in warm clothes, but instead of wearing a hat – a hat is totally fine – he was wearing a snood over his head, like this 20-year-old creative number 10.
It was as if he had have won the game at Chelsea on his own. Well, it was a long working day for him that day, I made sure.
He was helping our kit men, and from now on he stays in shorts and t-shirt until the end of January on the pitch outside.

If anyone thinks ‘we are too good for this’ and can be cool like a 20-year-old number 10, like one of my staff members, I will make sure that everyone is also back to work and doesn’t enjoy himself too much.
But I don’t have to do anything with our supporters. They can even come with a snood over their head and enjoy themselves, no problem at all.
The Yorkshire Post said Farke was half-jokingly horrified earlier in the season when Ao Tanaka wore gloves in training before the weather had turned cold.
Some Optas for tonight’s Premier League game. They don’t make great reading for either side!
● Since a run of three consecutive wins in April/May last season (the third of which was against Chelsea), Nottingham Forest have won just two of their last 14 Premier League games (D5 L7).

● Since the start of March, no side has lost more Premier League games than Chelsea (13), while among ever present sides only Crystal Palace (17) have earned fewer points than the Blues in that time (23).

Fifa news via Nick Ames: a number of past and present Fifa employees have received letters requesting they attend interviews for a congressional investigation into the global governing body sparked by the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal.
Letters were sent on Wednesday to a number of staff along with a handful of former employees who held senior positions.

They have been asked by Democrats on the House judiciary committee to give evidence as efforts gather pace to examine Gianni Infantino’s failed FFE scheme along with links between Fifa and the Trump administration.
Should recipients agree, the voluntary interviews could commence as soon as next week.
Five Levski Sofia supporters were taken to hospital after violence before last night’s Europa League game at Marseille . Both the French and Bulgarian presidents are blaming the home fans.
The lead-up to the match at the Stade Vélodrome was marred by confrontations in the stands between the two sets of fans, including the throwing of projectiles and flares.

French president Emmanuel Macron condemned “in the strongest possible terms... acts of violence targeting Bulgarian fans”, the Élysée Palace said. The Bulgarian president, Iliana Iotova, said it was “unacceptable” and “shocking”.

“The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world,” she said in a statement on Facebook. “Everyone should be able to support their team without being afraid for their safety.”
Macron spoke to his Bulgarian counterpart on the sidelines of a European summit in Brussels, assuring her that “these acts would not go unpunished”, the Élysée said.

Several hundred Marseille fans ran from the stand where they were situated about 10 minutes before kick-off, appearing to pursue a group of Bulgarian supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, where around 500 Levski fans were gathered.
“Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder,” the Marseille police prefecture told AFP. “Six others were treated on site for various wounds.” AFP

A week is a long time in football. With a midweek round of action in the Premier League , Manchester United could theoretically be somewhere in mid-table if their upcoming Saturday-Wednesday-Saturday schedule goes extremely well. Okay, that’s a big ask for a team without a top-flight win since (checks notes) August but home games against Brentford and Coventry either side of a midweek trip to Newcastle offer new boss Mauricio Pochettino the chance to build upon some promising signs in the 2-2 draw with Sporting.

Then again, United may be stranded at the bottom if it all goes belly up. The flurry of action begins tonight with Nottingham Forest hosting Chelsea and builds towards Sunday’s showdown at the Emirates where leaders Arsenal take on Manchester City.

Let’s stay in quiz mode. Plenty of football questions in our weekly offering. I got the first seven right and then fell apart – a bit like Manchester City.

He [Pochettino] is someone that we know. I studied his teams quite a lot in my coaching journey and had a lot of admiration for him. Even before his Tottenham team, it was his Southampton team.

Maybe I’m a good person, but I can also be a flower of evil. It’s the first time in my life I’ve realised this. I am a flower of evil, and I find it very beautiful.

articles.title: Manchester United extend Fernandes contract until 2028 to stop free transfer
articles.summary: Club activate option and plan further talks with captain ‘I am not nice,’ says Pochettino as he targets improvement Manchester United have triggered a clause to extend the captain Bruno Fernandes’s contract until the summer of 2028 on a day when Mauricio Pochettino warned his players they should not expect him to be “nice” in his attempts to turn around the club’s fortunes. Fernandes’s deal was due to expire in June and by exercising the option United have avoided the risk from January that he could negotiate a pre-contract agreement with a club abroad to join on a free next summer. Fernandes said this month that talks over a longer extension were on hold “because of the context of the team and the club”. He has turned down two United contract offers. Continue reading...
articles.content:
Manchester United have triggered a clause to extend the captain Bruno Fernandes’s contract until the summer of 2028 on a day when Mauricio Pochettino warned his players they should not expect him to be “nice” in his attempts to turn around the club’s fortunes.

Fernandes’s deal was due to expire in June and by exercising the option United have avoided the risk from January that he could negotiate a pre-contract agreement with a club abroad to join on a free next summer. Fernandes said this month that talks over a longer extension were on hold “because of the context of the team and the club”. He has turned down two United contract offers.

Immediate focus is on improving results, with United second-bottom of the Premier League with one win and also 19th in the Champions League standings. Fernandes is a doubt for Pochettino’s first home game in charge of United, against Brentford on Saturday, after missing training on Friday because of a virus.

Pochettino lost 4-0 at Liverpool in his first league game and followed that with a 2-2 draw at Sporting in the Champions League. He is confident of transforming the club and made clear he would not take a softly-softly approach.

“I am not nice,” he said. “I am trying to be good. But be careful, because we know when we need to push, when we need to be strong and when we need to build something to improve the atmosphere and relationship and everything. We have our experience and we are going to try to give everything to put the team, the club, the players on track again. And we really believe, we really believe that we can do it. It’s only a matter of time.”

If United beat Brentford it would be a first domestic win in 90 days. The performance against Sporting gave a vision of Pochettino’s plan to be aggressive and press high. The team have endured misfortune at the start of Pochettino’s tenure, having Leny Yoro wrongly sent off at Liverpool, according to a Football Association commission which rescinded the defender’s suspension , and two goals disallowed in Portugal.

“We need to accept that,” Pochettino said. “What are we going to do? Start to cry? No. Be strong, believe, keep going. I can think of many positive things in the two games. Maybe we didn’t win but for sure I think we are building our journey and for sure in the last seven, eight days we found a group of players, a group of staff, that want to help and want to be there, to help the team to perform and win games.”

Pochettino will be without the midfielder Carlos Baleba until late January but Marcus Rashford returned to individual training on Friday.

articles.title: Too old for soft toys? Tell that to kidults booking up the Harrods Jellycat cafe
articles.summary: Department stores are hosting in-person events for those who find comfort in collecting the British soft toy brand They’re cute, cuddly and taking over the homes of young adults. Jellycat, a British soft toy brand founded in 1999, is experiencing a rise in interest from adult buyers as they snap up signature smiley designs in the shape of everything from croissants and disco balls to turtles and teabags. Continue reading...
articles.content:
Department stores are hosting in-person events for those who find comfort in collecting the British soft toy brand

Jellycat, a British soft toy brand founded in 1999, is experiencing a rise in interest from adult buyers as they snap up signature smiley designs in the shape of everything from croissants and disco balls to turtles and teabags.

The trend is part of a wider “kidult” movement, with grownups buying items traditionally geared towards children, for example, Lego sets and Pokémon cards . On social media, videos of users talking through their collections of soft toys known as plushies can rack up millions of views.

On Monday, Harrods in London is opening “a first-of-its-kind dining destination” – a Jellycat cafe serving brunch in edible and soft toy form. Diners will be able to buy a peach granola bowl-shaped plushie, and eat the dish too.

According to research by Circana, “kidult” toy sales in the UK grew 22% in the first half of 2026. One in five toys and games are now bought by over-18s for themselves. At the US department chain Nordstrom, the average age of a Jellycat buyer is 27. Everything from nostalgia to a rise in anxiety disorders is being credited as a contributing factor to the trend.

Audrey Tang, a chartered member of the British Psychological Society, describes Jellycats as “tactile, comforting, calming and very cutesy”. She isn’t surprised to see increased demand from adults for plushies. “This year has been tough on a lot of people so if there is anything that makes us smile or makes us feel nice, we’re probably going to choose that,” she says.

Tang dismisses age-regression concerns, saying it is a type of judgment. “Try thinking about where that voice about rules is coming from,” she says. “Often those types of judgments come from parents or caregivers who have previously told us: ‘You’re too old for this or you should grow out of that.’”

Each Jellycat “character” is given a name by the brand and a brief bio. The toys hover around the £20 to £40 mark but discontinued or rare versions can fetch upwards of £500 on secondhand sites. Jellycat ranked fourth among the UK’s most-searched terms between January and September 2026, eBay reports. The Jellycat boom has also led to a rise in reports of “stealing to sell” shoplifting .

Bill Nighy has described himself as a “big, big Jellycat customer”. Sarah Jessica Parker has posted a photo of her own “Petal” bunny, while Kylie Jenner’s Jellycat of choice is a trio of green peas in a pod.

Mini bag charms, including 6cm-high pickles and marshmallows, are increasingly being spotted swinging from designer handbags.

Booking for the Harrods Jellycat brunch, which takes over a space previously occupied by the Prada cafe, opened in October and slots are sold out until February.

Rachel Dyer, 43, a business support officer, has booked a table to celebrate her 10th wedding anniversary. Dyer, who started collecting Jellycats in 2025, now has 95 plushies including a pine-cone tree, a fox, and a cat wearing a parka jacket. She describes her husband as being “bemused by the whole thing”.

Dyer says she likes how Jellycat allows her to embrace her inner child. “They bring me a little bit of comfort, joy and escapism, and I don’t think there’s anything wrong with that, whatever your age.”

The Harrods brunch follows other Jellycat in-person experiences, including a patisserie in Galeries Lafayette in Paris that sells small plush chouquettes (small choux buns) and a ranch in Texas that features a bald-eagle soft toy called Algernon. When Selfridges first launched its Fish and Chips Jellycat van last July, people queued for up to three hours to buy characters including a plush sausage and mushy peas wrapped in a bespoke newspaper.

Jellycat’s revenue jumped by 43% on the previous year to £450m, October figures show.

Tang says in-person events where people can meet fellow collectors help form wider connections. “Shared interests give people an instant talking point,” she says. “That can be a huge anxiety soother for someone who may be lonely or shy to talk to people. Why should we question anything that builds community in these divided times?”

articles.title: Renée Slegers leaves job as Arsenal Women’s coach after dismal run of results
articles.summary: Club languishing sixth in WSL after six home draws Held high hopes of mounting title challenge this term Renée Slegers has left her job as Arsenal Women’s head coach after a dismal set of results, with the club saying she has gone by mutual consent. The 37-year-old had been under contract until 2029 after signing a three-and-a-half-year deal in January but six consecutive home draws in the Women’s Super League this season have left Arsenal sixth, 12 points behind the leaders, Chelsea, and eight points adrift of a European place. Continue reading...
articles.content:
Renée Slegers has left her job as Arsenal Women’s head coach after a dismal set of results, with the club saying she has gone by mutual consent.

The 37-year-old had been under contract until 2029 after signing a three-and-a-half-year deal in January but six consecutive home draws in the Women’s Super League this season have left Arsenal sixth, 12 points behind the leaders, Chelsea, and eight points adrift of a European place.

Arsenal’s assistant coach Aaron D’Antino has also left, having been on the backroom staff since 2018. Arsenal’s director of women’s football, Clare Wheatley, told the club’s website a “change was necessary”, saying: “It was an extremely difficult decision to part ways with Renée, who has led the team with dedication and commitment throughout her time here.

“In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural Fifa Champions Cup, Renée has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal Football Club, with close support from Aaron. After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level, and change is necessary.”

Arsenal’s chief executive, Richard Garlick, described Slegers as a “wonderful person” but said a new head coach was required to give the club the best chance of meeting the ambition “to compete for and win major trophies consistently”.

It is understood Arsenal were determined to give Slegers time and so stood by her earlier in the season when speculation about her future was mounting but that eventually the two parties concluded a change was needed.

Arsenal’s search to find Slegers’ replacement is under way but it is understood the club will not rush to make an appointment, because their priority is to find the best person rather than ensuring somebody is in place for their next match, at Everton on 11 December in the WSL.

Melissa Clarke-Reed, the former Brighton and London City Lionesses head coach, has been placed in interim charge. The club are believed to be comfortable with her, if necessary, overseeing the three games that precede the winter break. Arsenal then return to action on 10 January.

Slegers took charge in October 2024, initially as interim head coach, after the resignation of Jonas Eidevall, under whom she had worked as an assistant. She oversaw a run of 10 wins in 11 matches without defeat in caretaker charge, prompting the club to appoint her as the head coach on an 18-month deal.

The Dutchwoman then led Arsenal to one of the greatest moments in their history as they won the Women’s Champions League title on 24 May 2025, stunning Barcelona with a surprise 1-0 victory in Lisbon to land the club’s second European title and their first for 18 years.

The 2025-26 season ended with Arsenal second in the WSL, four points behind the champions, Manchester City. They were semi-finalists in the Champions League and League Cup and quarter-finalists in the FA Cup, but Slegers won – on home soil – the inaugural Fifa Women’s Champions Cup , a competition between the winners of the respective continental titles.

Arsenal had held high hopes of mounting a WSL title challenge this term, vying to win their first domestic league title since 2019, and had what appeared to be a strong summer transfer window, signing high-calibre internationals such as the England midfielder Georgia Stanway and the Spain full-back Ona Batlle.

They have had injuries, including to their integral midfielder Mariona Caldentey, who is sidelined with a hamstring problem. The team’s inability to break down opponents set up in a low block has been a repetitive issue, and on Sunday there were loud boos at the Emirates when they were held to a goalless draw by West Ham.

Slegers, a former Netherlands midfielder, managed the Swedish club Rosengård and Sweden’s under-23s before joining Arsenal in 2023 to work under Eidevall.

articles.title: ‘We need to be ruthless’: Itoje issues England battle cry to make history against All Blacks
articles.summary: Hosts eye first ever treble of wins over New Zealand Captain wants ‘confrontational’ performance on Saturday Maro Itoje has called on his side to show their ruthless streak as they seek to become the first England side in history to clinch a third straight victory over New Zealand on Saturday. Itoje and co clinched a record 37-12 win over the forlorn All Blacks last Saturday and have been urged to go for the jugular with Steve Borthwick’s side hoping to round off their 2026 campaign with a sixth straight victory. Continue reading...
articles.content:
Maro Itoje has called on his side to show their ruthless streak as they seek to become the first England side in history to clinch a third straight victory over New Zealand on Saturday.

Itoje and co earned a record 37-12 win over the forlorn All Blacks last Saturday and have been urged to go for the jugular with Steve ­Borthwick’s side hoping to round off their 2026 campaign with a sixth consecutive victory.

New Zealand have an ever-growing injury list and are looking to avoid a sixth defeat of the year as they return to Twickenham with Codie Taylor, Will Jordan, Tupou Vaa’i and Anton Lienert-Brown all missing from the side that was downed last weekend. The head coach, Dave Rennie, has said he wants to show some “light at the end of the tunnel” before ending their most disappointing northern tour in recent memory.

“We always want to be ruthless,” said Itoje. “We want to be ­aggressive. We want to be the confrontational team on Saturday. But we’ll be fools to think that the All Blacks aren’t going to come out firing and come out with an aggressive mindset for themselves. But for us, of course, we need to be physical. We need to be aggressive. We need to be ­ruthless. All of those things. If I were to speak to you guys after the game, if I could describe our team in those three words, we would have had a great game.

“We’re playing the All Blacks. We’re playing the All Blacks in what essentially is a type of final. It’s going to be a hotly contested game. If we want to win, then we have to show up.”

Of the potential to beat New ­Zealand for the third time in a row, he added: “It is something that we can aim to do and aim to move ­forward with. That’s important and I would love to achieve that. But again I’m thinking about the direction of travel for this team.”

Saturday’s showdown with New ­Zealand is England’s 12th match of the year. They began with a Six Nations victory over Wales , which was a 12th win in a row, but slumped to five straight defeats thereafter. Since July’s loss against South Africa , however, Borthwick’s side have won their last five matches.

“We started the year with the Six Nations not how we wanted to,” added Itoje. “But I think this team has just stayed consistent. We stuck at it over the summer and made progress, and we’re making progress now. I think there’s just a lot of buy-in. We have definitely stayed together as a team. There is a collective spirit within the group, we have a good opportunity here, let’s pull it together.”
